level1.p1: A long time ago, in 1912, Nestori was summoned to face a grave task. An accident had struck at sea—one ship had already sunk, lost to a fatal signal error.
level1.p2: Now it fell to him to prevent further tragedy, to guide the remaining ships safely through the darkness and onto the shore.
level1.p3: Before him stood the lighthouse, long abandoned yet defiant against time. Its towering silhouette loomed into the night, nearly swallowed by the darkness, as if the sea itself were trying to erase it.
level1.p4: It had belonged to his family for hundreds of years. And now it was his turn to light it again.

level2.p1: Nestori felt a quiet pride as his first task came to an end. The sea had spared them, for now.
level2.p2: He couldn’t help but wonder how different it had been before his time. How dangerous the sea was already back then.
level2.p3: He moved slowly through the lighthouse, his footsteps echoing in the hollow silence. Near a window, something caught his eye - piece of old looking paper resting in the dust.
level2.p5: In the upper corner of the page, a single date was written: 1840.

level3.p1: Nestori had a feeling this was not the whole story. Not even close.
level3.p2: He tried to look for more pages in the dim glow of his miserable excuse for an oil lamp, which seemed to be doing its best not to help.
level3.p4: Just as his patience began to wear thin, he noticed a few pages scattered across the wooden floor.
level3.p5: He picked them up and held them closer to the flickering light.
level3.p6: Now they were filled with weird symbols Nestori didn’t recognize. And a date: 1790.
level3.p7: “Oh good,” Nestori sighed. “Now it’s getting ancient.”

level4.p1: “That was rather interesting“ he thought out loud. He flipped to the next page and it had those same mysterious symbols on it.
level4.p2: The date wasn’t far from the previous one: 1740

level5.p1: Nestori let out a sigh he hadn’t realized he’d been holding. The more pages he read, the worse the past seemed to get.
level5.p3: Clearly, the only sensible thing to do was find more pages and make it even worse.
level5.p4: He headed upstairs - and, to his mild disappointment, it didn’t even take a miracle to find exactly what he was looking for.

level6.p1: Nestori eventually noticed the weather had turned worse during his reading. The wind rattled the windows, and the rain had thickened into a solid wall - conveniently blocking out any possible escape.
level6.p2: He felt a strange knot tighten in his stomach.
level6.p3: “Perfect,” he muttered. “Exactly the sort of night one wants for reading cursed history.”
level6.p4: He hesitated, staring at the next page as if it might bite him.

level7.p1: “Wait, stop, HAHAHA I’m not qualified for this many limbs!”
level7.p2: The laughter echoed long after it stopped belonging to Nestori, rising and falling with the slow breath of the sea.
level7.p3: The light kept turning, steady as ever, sweeping across the water with careful precision.
level7.p4: Ships still saw it from afar and adjusted their course, trusting it as they always had.
level7.p5: Little did they know, the sea was hosting a gathering.
level7.p6: And Nestori had become a very good steward for the ocean.
